CNET has published a series of articles comparing the iPhone Duo against three existing Android foldables. While it takes a few separate comparisons to get the full picture, it's clear that the site sees Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold 8 as the device the Duo really needs to beat.

That conclusion is largely due to both phones adopting a similar passport-shaped aspect ratio, rather than the taller, narrower approach taken by other foldables, and they're only $100 apart in price…

Dimensions

Samsung's device is slightly thinner whether folded or unfolded.

Folded Unfolded iPhone Duo 11.3mm 5.2mm Fold 8 9.7mm 4.5mm

Dust resistance

One of the long-standing issues with early Samsung foldables was their tendency to be damaged by dust and debris, and the Fold 8 still carries this weakness. Its IP48 rating means it is fully water-resistant, but only protects against anything bigger than a grain of sand. The iPhone Duo, by contrast, is rated as fully water- and dust-resistant.

Cameras

The main cameras on both are fairly close on paper. The Duo has a 48-megapixel main shooter and an ultrawide, while the Fold 8 has a 50-megapixel main. Neither phone has a telephoto lens.

The Fold 8 has a 10-megapixel selfie camera built into the cover display, while the Duo has a 12-megapixel version. Samsung also packs a second 10-megapixel selfie camera into the inner display; Apple hasn't published specs for this part, but the fact that it supports 1080p video but not 4K suggests it's a much lower-resolution sensor.

Battery

As usual, Apple hasn't published the battery capacity, so that will have to wait for a teardown. The company does say it can last up to 24 hours of typical use.

The Fold 8 has faster wired charging, claiming to go from 0% to 73% in 30 minutes, while Apple says the Duo can hit 50% in the same time. Apple does have the edge in wireless charging, however, thanks to full MagSafe support, while the Fold 8 lacks the magnets needed to align with Qi2 wireless charging.

9to5Mac's take

In reality, of course, most people want to stay within their existing ecosystem, whether that's Apple or Android. Cross-platform comparisons only really matter when one side's device is compelling enough to lure users away from the other.

My own guess is that the iPhone Duo is more likely than most iPhones to attract Android users who want a foldable. Samsung's track record on durability has been less than stellar, which could be a deciding factor when shopping for such an expensive device — the Fold 8 is priced at $1,900 versus $1,999 for the Duo. On top of that, even Android fans seem to gush about the aesthetics of Apple's user interface.
